sections.h2: Who sets and collects property tax in Texas?
sections.html:
Local governments do. The Comptroller states that Texas has no state property tax, so counties, cities, school districts and special districts each set a rate and tax the same house.

An appraisal district values the property as of January 1, and a tax assessor-collector, often the county's, usually bills and collects for many units at once. Appraisal districts do not levy tax. Their chief appraiser also processes exemptions, and an appraisal review board hears disputes.

sections.h2: What is the yearly Texas property tax calendar?
sections.html:
The cycle starts on January 1 and ends with delinquency the next year. The table lists the dates as the Comptroller prints them.

Texas property tax calendar from the Comptroller's deadlines page
DateWhat happens
January 1Value, exemption qualification and the tax lien are set for the year
April 1 or soon afterValue notices for single-family homesteads
April 30Last day to file many exemption applications
May 1 or soon afterValue notices for other property
May 15Last day to protest with the review board, or 30 days after the notice, whichever is later
July 25Chief appraiser certifies the roll to each taxing unit
September 29Last day for most units to adopt a rate, or within 60 days of the certified roll if later
October 1Assessor mails bills
November 30 and June 30Split payment halves, where allowed
January 31Last day to pay without delinquency

The Comptroller says bills go out in October and payment is due on receipt, with delinquency starting February 1 for taxes unpaid after January 31.

sections.h2: How are Texas tax rates set?
sections.html:
Each unit adopts its own rate after a notice and hearing process. The Comptroller's truth-in-taxation page says most units must calculate a no-new-revenue rate and a voter-approval rate once they receive the certified roll.

The no-new-revenue rate is a comparison rate that would raise the same tax from the same properties as last year. The voter-approval rate is the highest rate allowed without an election. For most units other than schools it allows about the same operating revenue as the year before plus an extra 3.5 percent, plus enough for debt payments. Special taxing units, such as junior college and hospital districts, get an extra 8 percent for operations. If a unit adopts a rate above the voter-approval rate, voters decide at the next uniform election date.

  • Taxing units publish both calculated rates on their websites.
  • Most units file a notice that gives the meeting date and time.
  • Units other than very small ones hold one public hearing.

sections.h2: When do Texas property taxes become delinquent, and what do penalties look like?
sections.html:
Taxes unpaid on February 1 are delinquent, and the collector adds a 6 percent penalty plus 1 percent interest that day. The Comptroller's payment page then has the penalty growing 1 percent each month until July 1, when it reaches 12 percent, with interest running 1 percent per month and no cap.

Units with attorney contracts may add up to 20 percent more for collection. The bill must give at least 21 days after mailing, so a bill mailed after January 10 pushes delinquency to the first day of a later month. The page prints an example of a bill mailed January 15 turning delinquent March 1.

  • Penalty and interest can be waived in some cases if the tax is paid by the 21st day after the owner learns of the delinquency and the request is in writing before the 181st day after the delinquency date.
  • Some collectors offer installment plans up to 36 months on delinquent tax, and one is required on a residence homestead.
  • Homeowners 65 or older, or disabled, may pay in four installments.

sections.h2: Which exemptions lower a Texas homeowner's bill?
sections.html:
The main one is the residence homestead exemption. School districts must give $140,000, and any unit may adopt a local option exemption of up to 20 percent of value, not less than $5,000, per the Comptroller's exemptions page.

  • Age 65 or older, or disabled: an extra $60,000 school district exemption, plus any local option exemption.
  • Disabled veterans: amounts from $5,000 to $12,000 depending on the rating, and a full exemption on the homestead of a 100 percent disabled veteran.
  • A surviving spouse 55 or older may keep a deceased spouse's over-65 benefit in certain cases.

The application usually goes to the appraisal district before May 1. A buyer who takes a house after January 1 may claim the exemption for the rest of that year right away if the previous owner did not have one.

sections.h2: What limits how fast a homestead tax bill can rise?
sections.html:
A homestead appraisal cap limits value growth to 10 percent a year, starting the year after the exemption is first qualified, according to the Comptroller's appraisal limits page. The cap applies to appraised value, and new improvements can raise it.

Owners 65 or older, or disabled, also get a school tax ceiling, often called a freeze. A school district may not raise the total tax on that homestead above the amount tied to the year the owner qualified, and the ceiling can move proportionately to a new Texas homestead. Counties, cities and junior college districts may adopt a similar limit.

sections.h2: Can you dispute an appraisal or appeal after a protest?
sections.html:
Yes. File with the appraisal review board by May 15 or 30 days after the notice, whichever is later. After the board rules, the next steps are state district court, regular binding arbitration or, for values above $1,000,000, the State Office of Administrative Hearings.

An owner who appeals must pay the undisputed tax before the delinquency date. For a fuller walkthrough, see our Texas property tax protest guide.

sections.h2: How are property taxes handled when you sell a Texas house?
sections.html:
The tax lien attaches on January 1 each year, so the lien follows the property and a title company will not let a closing skip an unpaid year. The Comptroller notes the owner on January 1 stays liable for that year's tax and can be sued even after selling.

The closing statement usually pays unpaid tax from the seller's proceeds and splits the current year between seller and buyer. Ask the tax office for the current balance by account number and ask the title company how the proration will be shown.

  • Ask the tax assessor-collector for a tax certificate showing all taxing units.
  • Check for delinquent years, penalties and attorney fees.
  • Move any homestead exemption benefit to the buyer's name after closing.

faqs.q: Does Texas have a state property tax?
faqs.a: No. The Comptroller says Texas has no state property tax, and local taxing units set rates and collect the tax.

faqs.q: When are Texas property taxes due?
faqs.a: Bills go out in October with payment due on receipt, and taxes unpaid after January 31 are delinquent on February 1. Split payment lets some owners pay half by November 30 and half by June 30.

faqs.q: What penalty applies to late Texas property taxes?
faqs.a: A 6 percent penalty and 1 percent interest are added on February 1. The penalty rises 1 percent per month until July 1, when it reaches 12 percent.

faqs.q: How much is the Texas homestead exemption?
faqs.a: School districts must give $140,000 on a residence homestead, with another $60,000 for owners 65 or older or disabled. Other units may adopt local exemptions.

faqs.q: Can unpaid property taxes be paid at closing?
faqs.a: Yes. Unpaid tax is generally settled from the seller's proceeds through the title company, since the tax lien stays with the property.
